name: Q-switched / picosecond laser for dark circles

lead: Q-switched and picosecond lasers deliver extremely short, intense pulses of light. In dermatology they treat tattoos, dark spots and other pigmentation, and people apply the idea to periorbital hyperpigmentation, the brown-pigment type of dark circle, to lighten it.

Q-switching stores energy in the laser and releases it as one short pulse; in tattoo work the pulses shatter ink into particles the body clears, and the same physics is applied to pigment. Nd:YAG types are the most commonly favoured. A picosecond laser was introduced in 2013 for hard-to-remove inks. Periorbital hyperpigmentation is described as an inherited trait of extra melanin, most prevalent at ages 16 to 25. No published studies of these lasers for dark circles were located.

paras: Clinicians perform it in a clinic, typically as a series of sessions. It is discussed for pigment-type dark circles rather than those caused by hollows or visible vessels.
The sources reviewed do not discuss side effects. Periorbital skin is thin and close to the eye, so laser procedures there are done by clinicians.

angle.text: Users look to these dermatology pigment lasers to lighten brown-pigment dark circles. Short pulses break up pigment under the eye so the area looks lighter. The lasers are established for tattoos and pigmentation; published under-eye evidence is limited.

lead: Q-switched and picosecond lasers are short-pulse lasers used in dermatology to treat tattoos and pigmentation. In appearance communities they are discussed as a treatment for periorbital hyperpigmentation, the dark-pigment type of under-eye circles.

Q-switching produces short, intense pulses by blocking feedback in the laser cavity while energy accumulates, then releasing it at once [1]. Q-switched lasers, with Nd:YAG types the most commonly favored, are used for tattoo removal and also to treat dark spots and other pigmentation problems [1]. A picosecond laser was introduced in 2013 for hard-to-clear inks, according to Wikipedia, which does not cite a source for the claim [1].

Periorbital hyperpigmentation is described as an inherited trait of extra melanin, most prevalent at ages 16 to 25 [2]. No published studies of these lasers for dark circles were located for this article.

paras: In active Q-switching an external switch controls release of stored laser energy; in passive Q-switching a saturable absorber does so. Compared with mode locking, Q-switching yields lower repetition rates and higher pulse energy [1]. In tattoo treatment the pulses fragment ink particles that the lymphatic system removes, and full removal typically takes many sessions spaced at least a month apart [1].

People who discuss under-eye darkness as a hardmaxxing topic list pigment lasers alongside peels and microneedling as options for periorbital pigment. No community thread material was available for this article, so specific claims are not documented here.

timeline.event: Picosecond tattoo laser introduced, per Wikipedia (uncited there) [1].
